In addition to releasing the macOS 27.2 Golden Gate public beta 2, Apple also began rolling out the first release candidates of macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.2 today. Details are as follows.

Older versions of macOS continue to receive security updates

As is typical for minor updates to older macOS versions, Apple today released the first release candidates of macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.2, without first issuing a standard beta version.

Apple released macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 at the end of last month, and both versions went through two release candidates before their official launch.

The release notes accompanying the first release candidates of macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.2 simply state that the update "provides important security fixes and is recommended for all users to install." Last month's update contained a CoreGraphics security fix, described as follows:

Apple is expected to release the details of the fixes included in macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.2 after their official release, which is anticipated to be within the next few weeks, alongside macOS 27.2 Golden Gate.

The build number for macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 Release Candidate 1 is 24H219, while the build number for macOS Tahoe 26.7.2 Release Candidate 1 is 25G320.

Have you noticed any new features or changes in today's release candidate? Let us know in the comments.
